To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we can use blockchains to implement certificate revocation lists that are reliable, secure and efficient.
we propose a solution for CRL management that is based on a blockchain-based ledger and is resilient to failures of CAs and CRLs, and is secure in the presence of a malicious CA.

(a) we propose a new, distributed model for CRL maintenance based on public ledgers and blockchains; (b) we design a protocol that allows CAs to share a public, robust and reliable ledger of CRLs; (c) we prove that the protocol is secure, and that the shared ledger is resilient to attacks and failures of CAs; (d) we show that our solution can be implemented with existing blockchain technologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: can a public blockchain be used to improve the security of a CA-based PKI?

(i) a new model for certificate-based authentication, where multiple CAs share the maintenance of CRLs; (ii) a new model of public ledger, where CRLs of different CAs are collected in an immutable, distributed and robust data structure, the blockchain; (iii) an implementation of a prototype system based on the Ethereum blockchain platform.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blockchain is a technology that can provide a secure and reliable infrastructure for certificate validation and revocation.
blockchain-based CRLs are a viable and effective solution to the POF of CRL availability and authenticity.
the blockchain-based solution for CRLs is a viable solution for the CRL POF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new, decentralized, robust and efficient model for the management of certificate revocation in PKIs, based on blockchains.
we have designed and implemented a blockchain-based CRL management solution that is robust and efficient, and that can be easily adopted by existing PKIs.
we have designed, implemented and evaluated a solution that provides an efficient and reliable way to maintain CRLs, by exploiting the blockchain technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
blockchains can be used as public ledgers to collect, in a decentralized way, CRLs for multiple CAs and to make them available and authentic to any entity that needs to validate certificates.
blockchains can be used as a robust and secure infrastructure for the management and validation of certificate revocations.
blockchains can be successfully used for the purpose of CRLs, with several benefits.
